choices.misconception: I treated $0.6 \div 0.03$ as $0.6 \div 3 = 0.2$, ignoring the decimal point in the bottom number, then added $0.6 \div 0.3 = 2$ to get $2.2$.
I ignored every decimal point and just divided the digits, $6 \div 3 = 2$ for each fraction, so I got $2 + 2 = 4$.
I got $0.6 \div 0.03 = 20$ right, but I thought $0.6 \div 0.3 = 0.2$, so I added to get $20.2$.
I moved the decimal points one place too far in both fractions, getting $200$ and $20$, so I added to get $220$.

hints: Dividing by a decimal is easier if you first make the bottom number a whole number.
Multiply the top and bottom of each fraction by the same power of $10$: $\dfrac{0.6}{0.03} = \dfrac{60}{3}$ and $\dfrac{0.6}{0.3} = \dfrac{6}{3}$.
$\dfrac{60}{3} = 20$ and $\dfrac{6}{3} = 2$. Now add the two results.

solutions.reliable: Multiplying the top and bottom of a fraction by the same number does not change its value. So $\dfrac{0.6}{0.03} = \dfrac{60}{3} = 20$ (multiply both by $100$) and $\dfrac{0.6}{0.3} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2$ (multiply both by $10$). The sum is $20 + 2 = 22$.
solutions.elegant: The bottom of the first fraction is $10$ times smaller than the bottom of the second, so the first fraction is $10$ times bigger. Since $\dfrac{0.6}{0.3} = 2$, the first is $20$, and the total is $22$.
